 Spurs-Jazz injury report: Fox’s hip tightness and the Jazz’s depleted frontcourt 
 Fox may not suit up. By Jahlil Williams | Nov 15, 2026, 2:51 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Nov 9, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) against the Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect De'Aaron Fox popped up as a late addition to the Spurs' injury report for their third meeting of the season with Utah. San Antonio is 2-0 against the Jazz, and should easily secure a third win for their 12th straight victory—the longest streak in the NBA. Their opponent is bruised and battered with their best player out and their frontcourt decimated .

 I don't know that we should expect another 38-point clobbering like they did to the Warriors on Friday, but nobody would be shocked by it either. Take out their five-point victory in Chicago, and the Spurs have won four of their last five games by an average of 25.3 points.

 The Jazz were projected to be a breakout team this season, but reality has been much crueler. The injury bug hit them early, and it's been relentless ever since. Coach Will Hardy's club has only won one game nearly a month into the new campaign. 
--> The Jazz were projected to be a breakout team this season, but reality has been much crueler. The injury bug hit them early, and it's been relentless ever since. Coach Will Hardy's club has only won one game nearly a month into the new campaign. 
 Utah has the 29th-ranked offensive rating, the 25th-ranked defensive rating, and the 28th-ranked net rating. Realistically, there's no reason for this team to hang around with the Spurs if they're locked in from the beginning.

 Victor Wembanyama has averaged 24 points, 12.5 rebounds, five assists, and 2.5 blocks across two games versus the Jazz this season. The split was wider than those numbers suggest, though. 
--> Victor Wembanyama has averaged 24 points, 12.5 rebounds, five assists, and 2.5 blocks across two games versus the Jazz this season. The split was wider than those numbers suggest, though. 
 He had 36 poiints and 14 boards in an overtime win in the first meeting, but only 12 and 11 were needed in the second, as the Spurs blew Utah away , 119-97, with a group effort where seven players scored double-digits, which included a team-high 17-point contribution from Dylan Harper.
